raw_record.support_text: Richardson and Cunningham fed rats 3'-methyl-4-dimethylaminoazobenzene and liver tumors arose; fewer neoplasms of the liver developed in companion groups that also received small doses of the strong carcinogen 3-methylcholanthrene.
raw_record.extra_details: Hepatic tumor induction was inhibited when 3-methylcholanthrene, benzo[a]pyrene, benz[a]anthracene, or dibenz[a,h]anthracene was added to the diet.

raw_record.support_text: The liver tumors (primary carcinomas) were induced by the azo dye derivative 3'-methyl-4-dimethylaminoazobenzene, which was mixed with the rat diet at a concentration of 0.058 per cent; tumors were harvested after 3 to 5 months of carcinogen treatment, and only small, firm, grossly non-necrotic tumors were fractionated.
raw_record.extra_details: Azo dye derivative; mixed with diet at 0.058 per cent; tumors harvested after 3 to 5 months of treatment and only small, firm, grossly non-necrotic tumors were fractionated.

raw_record.support_text: The feeding of carcinogenic 3'-methyl-4-dimethylaminoazobenzene (3'-MeDAB) to rats leads to changes in the protein composition of liver nuclear ribonucleoprotein particles and induces hepatomas. The paper states that 'The induction of hepatomas by carcinogenic aminoazo dyes' is the context, and describes hepatomas induced by 3'-MeDAB, while noting the loss of a 42 000 MW polypeptide from the particles is not characteristic of the malignant transformation and this polypeptide is present in even higher proportion in hepatoma particles.
raw_record.extra_details: 3'-MeDAB described as carcinogenic; feeding caused a decrease then complete loss of a 42 000 apparent MW polypeptide from liver nuclear 30S ribonucleoprotein particles; 3'-MeDAB binds to the proteins of liver nuclear ribonucleoprotein particles and interferes with RNA processing; hepatoma induced by 3'-MeDAB contained this polypeptide in higher proportion than control liver particles.

raw_record.support_text: Rat hepatoma was generated after continuous feeding of a basal diet containing 0.06% 3'-methyl-4-dimethylaminoazobenzene (3'-Me-DAB) [146]. After 35 weeks of feeding, rats were killed and the tumorous and non-tumorous liver tissues were removed; in individual rats regucalcin mRNA expression in the tumorous tissues was generally decreased compared with the non-tumorous tissues of the chemical-fed rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Chemical also known as 3'-Me-DAB. Hepatoma induced by continuous feeding of basal diet containing 0.06% 3'-Me-DAB for 35 weeks. In the tumorous tissues regucalcin mRNA expression was decreased relative to non-tumorous tissues; Southern blotting showed no rearranged regucalcin gene band in the hepatoma, suggesting the regucalcin gene is not modified in this tumorigenesis; c-myc mRNA expression was specifically increased in the induced hepatomas.

raw_record.support_text: Cancer induction in rat liver was chosen as an experimental model. Feeding the carcinogen 3'-methyl-4-dimethylaminoazobenzene (3'-MeDAB) to rats results in a high incidence of cancer development; tumours usually became apparent from 10 to 12 weeks after the beginning of the treatment period.
raw_record.extra_details: Tumours usually became apparent from 10 to 12 weeks after the beginning of the feeding period. Stated as 'the carcinogen 3'-MeDAB'. Adenylate cyclase findings during pre-malignant stage: increased basal and isoprenaline-responsive adenylate cyclase, depressed glucagon-responsive adenylate cyclase.

raw_record.support_text: Azo-dye feeding to rats initially produces liver damage, followed by attempted regeneration through enhanced mitotic activity of hepatocytes, bile duct epithelium, and connective tissue cells, and culminates in the development of tumors arising from the liver parenchyma (hepatomas) or from bile ducts (cholangiomas). The text explicitly refers to the feeding of the carcinogen 3'-methyl-4-dimethylaminoazobenzene (DAB), which produced three parenchymal cell populations in preneoplastic liver, with hyperbasophilic cells considered the immediate precursors of the malignant hepatoma cells.
raw_record.extra_details: Alias DAB. Feeding produced three cell populations in preneoplastic liver (hypobasophilic, basophilic, hyperbasophilic); hyperbasophilic cells considered immediate precursors of malignant hepatoma cells; anomalous mitoses, extranuclear DNA, loss of DNase and RNase activity, enhanced DNA synthesis. Related non-specific azo-dye feeding claim also present in the text.

raw_record.support_text: In the marmoset, clofibrate (which produces liver tumors in the rat) did not produce any tumors in a 6 1/2-year study, which is around half the expected life span of this species.
raw_record.extra_details: Peroxisome proliferator that produces liver tumors in the rat; did not produce any tumors in the marmoset in a 6 1/2-year study.

raw_record.support_text: Clofibrate was tested for carcinogenicity by dietary administration in rats and mice, and in one experiment in marmosets by gastric instillation for 6.5 years. It induced Leydig-cell tumors in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Leydig-cell tumor is one component of the 'Tumor Triad'; this case study focuses on the liver tumor only, not the Leydig-cell tumor.

raw_record.support_text: Alachlor exposure produced small raised plaques that progress to elevated neoplastic polyps and finally to well-differentiated adenomas in the rat nasal cavity. Given the evolution of the lesions and multiplicity of masses, longer alachlor exposure is expected to progress the well-differentiated benign tumors to anaplastic adenomas and adenocarcinomas; a preliminary assessment of 2 rats fed an alachlor-containing diet for 10.5 and 11 months revealed multiple adenomas and an adenocarcinoma.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: well-differentiated adenomas of the nasal cavity
raw_record.extra_details: Alachlor is an herbicide. Benign lesions evolved from plaques to polyps to well-differentiated adenomas. Exposure-duration-related progression to anaplastic adenomas and adenocarcinomas was proposed.

raw_record.support_text: Data on health effects of the pre-emergence herbicide alachlor show adequate evidence for carcinogenicity. Rat feeding studies resulted in nasal turbinate tumors, thyroid follicular cell tumors and mixed gastric tumors. A structural relation of alachlor to other compounds that produce a similar spectrum of tumors also supports the weight of evidence for alachlor carcinogenicity. Studies in mice provided evidence of bronchioalveolar adenoma and combined adenoma/carcinoma, but the data were inconclusive. The pHG is calculated treating alachlor as a carcinogen using the non-linear approach.
raw_record.extra_details: The paper states adequate evidence for carcinogenicity; a structural relation to other compounds producing a similar tumor spectrum also supports the weight of evidence. PHG was calculated treating alachlor as a carcinogen via a non-linear approach (point of departure 0.5 mg kg-1 day-1, UF 1000, RSC 20%, 70 kg BW, 2 l day-1 water consumption), yielding a PHG of 4 ppb.

raw_record.support_text: At high doses, a reactive metabolite of tamoxifen covalently binds to cytochrome P450 and produces DNA adducts in rat liver microsomes; as a result, tamoxifen is considered a strong hepatocarcinogen in rats. The tolerability table also lists tamoxifen as 'tumourogenic in rats' for the liver.
raw_record.extra_details: Described as a 'strong hepatocarcinogen in rats'. Accompanying mechanistic observations: covalent binding to cytochrome P450 and formation of DNA adducts in rat liver microsomes; hepatic DNA adducts were not significantly detected in human liver biopsies.

raw_record.support_text: The carcinogenicity of tamoxifen in the rat liver is well established.
raw_record.extra_details: Described as well established in rat liver only.

raw_record.support_text: In the present two-stage rat mammary carcinogenesis bioassay, PhIP(+) control animals developed mammary fibroadenomas (45% incidence, multiplicity 0.8 +/- 1.2) and adenocarcinomas (80% incidence, multiplicity 2.0 +/- 1.9), for a total mammary tumor incidence of 85%. This positive result attributes induction of mammary neoplasms in intact rats to PhIP (2-Amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine).
raw_record.extra_details: Alias PhIP. Also induced benign mammary fibroadenomas (45% incidence). Administered under a two-stage initiation/post-initiation protocol; text indicates PhIP was given by intragastric injections. Associated with PhIP-DNA adduct formation in mammary gland, colon, and pancreas. The study evaluated chemopreventive effects of conjugated linoleic acid on this PhIP-induced carcinogenesis.

raw_record.support_text: The passage notes that when meats are cooked at high temperatures or broiled on charcoal grills, heterocyclic aromatic amine and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon carcinogens form. It specifically identifies the heterocyclic amine carcinogen 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP), which causes prostate cancer when fed to rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Heterocyclic amine carcinogen that forms when meats are cooked at high temperatures or broiled on charcoal grills.

raw_record.support_text: The passage identifies 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP) as a potent rat colon carcinogen. It reports that PhIP did not induce tumors in rat liver, that it is efficiently detoxified in the liver with extremely low levels of PhIP-DNA adducts, and that depletion of hepatocyte glutathione increased PhIP-DNA adduct formation 15-fold and produced high levels of unscheduled DNA synthesis.
raw_record.extra_details: Alias PhIP. Food-borne heterocyclic amine. Described as 'potent' colon carcinogen in rats; efficiently detoxified in liver with low PhIP-DNA adducts; GSH depletion raised PhIP-DNA adducts 15-fold; glucuronidation inhibition (D-galactosamine) increased DNA adducts and unscheduled DNA synthesis 2-fold.

raw_record.support_text: Shirai et al. showed that the heterocyclic amine, 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP), produced prostate cancer when fed to rats.
raw_record.extra_details: PhIP is a heterocyclic amine produced from cooking meats (broiling/frying of meats and fish); it is the major contributor to estimated daily heterocyclic amine intake in the US population (approximately 70% of total mean intake).

raw_record.support_text: Among the ten heterocyclic aromatic amines proven carcinogenic in experimental animals, 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP) is considered a major risk factor for colon cancer because it is mutagenic in bacterial and mammalian genotoxicity assays and induces colon tumors in rats (Ito et al. 1991).
raw_record.extra_details: Alias PhIP; HCA abundantly formed in meat cooked at high temperature; induces colon tumors in rats (Ito et al. 1991); mutagenic in genotoxicity assays.

raw_record.support_text: PhIP (2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine), a heterocyclic aromatic amine formed when cooking meat at high temperature, was translated into experimental colorectal cancer: rats fed PhIP had a 50% incidence of colonic tumors, and PhIP combined with a high-fat diet or AOM enhances tumorigenesis.
raw_record.extra_details: Rats fed PhIP had a 50% incidence of colonic tumors; PhIP combined with a high-fat diet or AOM enhances tumorigenesis; heterocyclic aromatic amine formed during high-temperature meat cooking.

raw_record.support_text: The paper examines miRNA profiles altered in rat colon tumors induced by 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP), which is described in the scope as a heterocyclic amine carcinogen from cooked meat. PhIP was used to induce colon tumors in rats as the model system for the study.
raw_record.extra_details: Heterocyclic amine carcinogen from cooked meat. PhIP was used to induce colon tumors in rats in this systems-biology study of miRNA alterations.

raw_record.support_text: Experimental studies support a pro-carcinogenic role of red and processed meat in breast cancer development; these foods contain mutagenic by-products, among which the heterocyclic amine 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and N-nitroso compounds, that stimulate mammary carcinogenesis in experimental studies. The paper additionally notes that PhIP-induced mammary carcinogenesis in rats has been experimentally demonstrated (mechanistic data from animal models).
raw_record.extra_details: PhIP is the most prevalent heterocyclic amine in red/processed meat; exposure occurs via meat processing or preparation (cooking). Dietary antioxidant supplementation (α-tocopherol or synthetic ascorbic acid derivatives) exerts a chemopreventive action against PhIP-induced mammary carcinogenesis in rats.

raw_record.support_text: Among the heterocyclic amines, 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP) has been shown to induce colon tumors in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Also called PhIP; heterocyclic amine in cooked foods; induced nine colon tumors in F344 rats in this study; humans exposed at ~3-12 ug/d.

raw_record.support_text: In animal feeding studies, PhIP produced elevated colon cancer incidence in male rats (16/29 vs 0/40 controls), supporting induction of colon cancer by PhIP.
raw_record.extra_details: Full name 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo-[4,5-b]-pyridine; dose 2.1 mg/kg/day; incidence shown as number with tumor/total alive at first death.

raw_record.support_text: Studies in rats treated by orally administered benzo[a]pyrene (B[a]P) confirm its mammary carcinogenicity. B[a]P is probably the most extensively studied of the PAH carcinogens.
raw_record.extra_details: Most extensively studied of the PAH carcinogens; present in cigarette smoke at about 9 ng/cigarette in mainstream smoke of full flavor cigarettes.

raw_record.support_text: Three of the four PAHs tested for carcinogenicity in rats after oral exposure, namely benz[a]anthracene, benzo[a]pyrene and dibenz[a,h]anthracene, are carcinogenic.
raw_record.extra_details: One of three PAHs that were carcinogenic when tested for carcinogenicity in rats after oral exposure.

raw_record.support_text: Tumours were induced in rats by feeding them on a diet containing 0·06% of 4-dimethylaminoazobenzene as described by Campbell (1955).
raw_record.extra_details: Compound fed in diet at 0.06%; tumours induced in rats; also referred to as N,N-dimethylaminoazobenzene (butter yellow). Also used in the paper as a method to produce liver tumours for subsequent radioisotope-labelling studies; a rat bearing such liver tumours was later injected with [14C]alanine and [14C]lysine-labelled albumin.

raw_record.support_text: Liver tumours arise following the administration of butter yellow (4-dimethylaminoazobenzene). When fed to rats, the dye becomes bound to certain proteins in liver cells, and later the tumours that develop can be shown to lack the capacity to bind the dye (Miller and Miller, 1947).
raw_record.extra_details: Also known as butter yellow. The dye binds to certain proteins in liver cells and developing tumours lack the capacity to bind the dye, attributed to deletion of the dye-binding protein(s).

raw_record.support_text: The paper states that the carcinogenic properties of nuclear and N-methylated derivatives of 4-amino-azobenzene are well known, and that 4-Dimethylaminoazobenzene (Butter Yellow) in particular is notable for the high yield of malignant hepatomata it produces when fed to rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Alias: Butter Yellow. Studied by Miller, Miller and Baumann (1945) at the McArdle Memorial Laboratory, Madison, USA; also found to combine chemically with liver protein. High yield of malignant hepatomata.

raw_record.support_text: Primary carcinoma of the liver, readily induced in rats by feeding p-dimethylaminoazobenzene, is a tumor well suited to biochemical study. In such animals the biotin level of the liver adjacent to the neoplasms was found to be normal, while the carcinomas themselves were decidedly poorer in this factor; e.g., controls 3671 and 3190 my, tumors 1905 and 812 my of biotin. This discrepancy can not be explained by the presence of necrosis, for all visible necrotic material was removed.
raw_record.extra_details: The liver carcinomas were observed to be poorer in biotin than adjacent normal liver tissue (controls 3671 and 3190 my; tumors 1905 and 812 my of biotin), a finding not explained by necrosis.

raw_record.support_text: Rats fed a diet containing p-dimethylaminoazobenzene developed hepatic tumors after 125 to 150 days on the diet. Some tumors showed morphological changes usually associated with malignant neoplasms and appeared to be actively infiltrating surrounding tissues; other livers showed only fibrosis with bile-duct proliferation resembling cholangiomas. The diet is referred to as a carcinogenic diet.
raw_record.extra_details: p-Dimethylaminoazobenzene (butter yellow) fed in the diet; hepatic tumors observed after 125-150 days; also described as a 'carcinogenic diet' and 'the carcinogen' in the text. Three-fourths of rats killed after six months on the diet had hepatic tumors. Some livers showed fibrosis with bile-duct proliferation resembling cholangiomas.

raw_record.support_text: SUGIURA fed rats for 60 days on p-dimethylaminoazobenzene (butter yellow) in a brown rice diet, in order to induce liver tumors, and then transferred the animals onto dye-free rations. The incidence of liver neoplasms was significantly lower in rats given yeast or milk powder supplements, while the azo-dye butter yellow itself was administered to induce liver tumors.
raw_record.extra_details: Study by SUGIURA; rats fed 60 days on azo-dye (butter yellow) in a brown rice diet to induce liver tumors, then shifted to dye-free rations. Incidence of liver neoplasms was significantly lower with yeast or milk powder supplementation; riboflavin and B-vitamins are reported to reduce the carcinogenicity of azo-dyes through hepatic xenobiotic-metabolizing enzymes.

raw_record.support_text: Wilson, De Eds & Cox (1941) found that continued oral administration of 2-acetamidofluorene to rats produced tumours of several organs, notably the bladder, liver and lungs. Morris & Eyestone (1953) obtained bladder tumours with it in dogs. Its versatility as a carcinogen was confirmed by later work reviewed by Bielschowsky (1947).
raw_record.extra_details: Compound of interest for its insecticidal properties; never manufactured on a large scale because of its carcinogenic action. Carcinogenicity further confirmed by Bielschowsky (1947), studied by the Millers and Morris and co-workers.

raw_record.support_text: Hyperplastic liver nodules and hepatocellular carcinomas were induced in rats by oral administration of the carcinogen N-2-fluorenylacetamide. The development of the tumors was slow, and FOR the study, neoplastic tissue was compared with control, fetal, neonatal, and precancerous liver tissues.
raw_record.extra_details: N-2-fluorenylacetamide, explicitly described as 'the carcinogen'; also induced hyperplastic liver nodules (preneoplastic lesions) in the same rats. Ganglioside sialic acid levels were elevated in all but the most poorly differentiated tumors.

raw_record.support_text: There have been many reports documenting enhancement of tumor formation in animals by antioxidants, and carcinogenic activity of BHA (butylated hydroxyanisole) itself was demonstrated in the rat forestomach.
raw_record.extra_details: BHA is an antioxidant; its carcinogenic activity in the forestomach is contrasted with its chemopreventive inhibition of chemical carcinogenesis in other organs.

raw_record.support_text: Butylated hydroxyanisole (BHA), an antioxidant used in foodstuffs and cosmetics, had its safety questioned when a Japanese carcinogenicity study reported that 2% BHA in a pelleted diet caused hyperplasia, papillomas and squamous cell carcinomas in forestomachs of rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Japanese carcinogenicity study; 2% BHA in a pelleted diet; hyperplasia also reported at the same forestomach site; the finding raised safety concerns about BHA.

raw_record.support_text: In the three-generation study detailed in the Oral Toxicity section of this report, no evidence of carcinogenicity was found in rats that were fed up to 2% Sodium Metabisulfite (Til, Feron, and DeGroot 1972a).
raw_record.extra_details: Three-generation study; rats fed up to 2% Sodium Metabisulfite (Til, Feron, and DeGroot 1972a).

raw_record.support_text: In the long-term study in rats (Til et al. 1972a) to which sodium metabisulphite was administered, there was no evidence of carcinogenicity.
raw_record.extra_details: Long-term dietary study (Til et al. 1972a); the compound was administered in thiamine-enriched diets under controlled storage.

raw_record.support_text: The study used hepatocellular carcinomas induced in rats by oral administration of N-nitrosomorpholine (NNM) as a model system. The NNM-induced rat HCCs showed significantly increased mRNA expression of protein phosphatase inhibitor-1, and findings indicate inhibitor-1 mRNA expression is linked to tumor progression and liver cell transformation.
raw_record.extra_details: NNM was used to induce hepatocellular carcinomas as a model for studying inhibitor-1 mRNA expression in rat hepatocarcinogenesis.

raw_record.support_text: In rats treated with the heterocyclic nitrosamine N-nitrosomorpholine (NNM), hepatocarcinogenesis was investigated in stop experiments. Sequence of cellular changes leads from glycogen-rich hepatocytes (glycogenosis) to basophilic hepatoma cells and hepatocellular tumors/carcinomas, and the relation of hepatocellular glycogenosis to the dosage and timing of carcinogenic treatment and to the development of hepatocellular tumors has been studied in detail.
raw_record.extra_details: Heterocyclic nitrosamine; stop experiments with 80, 120, 160 and 200 mg NNM/l drinking water for 7 weeks; hepatocarcinogenesis proceeds through preneoplastic glycogenotic/mixed/basophilic cell foci; proliferation increases in mixed and basophilic cell populations in foci, nodules, and carcinomas.

raw_record.support_text: In the present study, hepatocellular carcinomas were induced in rats by the hepatotropic carcinogen N-nitrosomorpholine (NNM) (Druckrey et al., 1967). During the induction phase and at the stage of hepatoma development, tissues were processed for subsequent cellular detection of AFP.
raw_record.extra_details: NNM is labeled a hepatotropic carcinogen per Druckrey et al., 1967. The aim was to localize cellular AFP by immunoperoxidase staining during NNM-induced hepatocarcinogenesis.

raw_record.support_text: Limonene, when administered in the diet at 1–5% mass, inhibits both 7,12-dimethylbenz[a]anthracene (DMBA)- and N-methyl-N-nitrosourea (MNU)-induced mammary carcinogenesis in rats, indicating that DMBA induces mammary carcinogenesis in this rat model.
raw_record.extra_details: DMBA was used here as a chemical mammary carcinogen; limonene administered in the diet inhibited the induced carcinogenesis.

raw_record.support_text: Table IV lists 7,12-Dimethylbenz[a]anthracene (DMBA) as the carcinogen producing breast neoplasia in the rat, inhibited by disulfiram, isothiocyanates, benzyl thiocyanate, and cysteamine. Paragraph 37 states disulfiram will inhibit mammary tumor formation in the rat resulting from oral administration of DMBA.
raw_record.extra_details: Mammary tumor formation resulted from oral administration of DMBA and was inhibited by disulfiram in the inhibition study.

raw_record.support_text: None of the control rats showed any tumor during necropsy, whereas DMBA-intubated rats developed nodules, about 83% of which were histologically verified to be mammary tumors. The study uses DMBA (7,12-dimethylbenz[a]anthracene), administered by intubation to rats, to induce mammary tumorigenesis across the dietary oil groups.
raw_record.extra_details: DMBA administered by intubation (gavage); rats were fed diets differing in fatty acid composition (high-linoleic safflower oil, high-oleic safflower oil, olive oil, olive oil + linoleic acid). About 83% of necropsy nodules were histologically verified as mammary tumors; the remainder included lobular hyperplasia/adenosis, enlarged lymph nodes, salivary glands, parotid gland adenomas/carcinomas, sebaceous gland carcinomas, thyroid adenocarcinomas, hibernomas, and foci of mastitis.

raw_record.support_text: DMBA (7,12-dimethylbenz[a]anthracene) exhibits selective cancer-inducing activity, in particular inducing mammary carcinoma in rats, and is used as a standard carcinogen in investigations on this type of cancer. The DMBA-induced neoplastic process is considered to involve formation of DNA adducts from active metabolites, induction of oxidative stress (decreased antioxidative enzymes such as catalase, superoxide dismutase, and glutathione peroxidase), blocking intestinal release of glutathione, and decreasing natural killer cell activity. The authors emphasize a negative effect of DMBA on the rat genome after even a single oral dose.
raw_record.extra_details: Used as a standard carcinogen (DMBA, 7,12-dimethyl-1,2-benz[a]anthracene) in mammary cancer research; proposed mechanisms include DNA adduct formation from active metabolites, oxidative stress with decreased catalase/superoxide dismutase/glutathione peroxidase, blocked intestinal glutathione release, and reduced natural killer cell activity. Negative effect on the rat genome reported after even a single oral dose. In this study rats fed the test diets had DMBA-induced mammary tumors first observed at 14 weeks of age, evaluated at 20 weeks.

raw_record.support_text: In rats, breast tumors can be induced by oral 7,12-dimethylbenz[a]anthracene (DMBA), with a near 100% latency period between 8 and 12 weeks. DMBA is described as a commonly used carcinogen shown to induce tumor formation in rats and mice, and DNA of parous animals was less susceptible to binding DMBA.
raw_record.extra_details: Also described as a commonly used carcinogen shown to induce tumor formation in rats and mice. Near 100% tumor induction with 8 to 12 week latency. Abbreviated DMBA; alias 7,12-dimethylbenz(a)anthracene. DNA in mammary epithelial cells of parous rats was less susceptible to binding DMBA.

raw_record.support_text: Neoplasms were found in the breast of rats at around 40 days after the application of DMBA (7,12-dimethylbenz[a]anthracene) by intragastric gavage. HE staining showed pathological dysplasia and interstitial fibrosis in the tissue of the DMBA group, indicating the breast cancer model on rats was successfully established.
raw_record.extra_details: DMBA was administered by intragastric gavage; neoplasms appeared around 40 days after application; HE staining showed pathological dysplasia and interstitial fibrosis in the DMBA group; used as an established rat breast cancer induction model (VPA intervention delayed and reduced tumor formation, which is a chemopreventive finding and excluded).

raw_record.support_text: Rats received an intragastric administration of DMBA (7,12-dimethylbenz[a]anthracene), which was used to induce rat mammary tumor development. The time-course study showed that by 120 days, due to the appearance and progression of tumors, a significant (p < 0.05) decrease in lymphocyte blastogenic activity was seen, although treatment with thymopentin (TP5) still ameliorated the immunosuppression.
raw_record.extra_details: DMBA administered intragastrically as a model carcinogen to induce rat mammary tumors; thymopentin (TP5, 100 ng/animal) given concurrently only modified immune responses and did not itself carry any carcinogenicity claim; tumor appearance/progression observed by 120 days.

raw_record.support_text: N-methyl-N-nitrosourea (MNU) induces mammary carcinogenesis in rats; dietary limonene at 1–5% mass inhibits this MNU-induced carcinogenesis.
raw_record.extra_details: MNU used here as a chemical mammary carcinogen; dietary limonene inhibited the induced carcinogenesis.

raw_record.support_text: The yield of mammary tumors induced in rats by N-methyl-N-nitrosourea was lowered by increasing dietary intakes of menhaden oil, whereas corn oil had the opposite effect. N-methyl-N-nitrosourea is reported as a chemical carcinogen producing mammary tumors in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Used as a chemical carcinogen in an induction model; the tumor yield was reduced by dietary menhaden oil and increased by corn oil.

raw_record.support_text: In the comparison of rat and human bladder lesions, the text notes that many rat bladder tumours at least focally assume an inverted (endophytic) growth pattern and that such tumours occur after treatment with MNU (N-methyl-N-nitrosourea).
raw_record.extra_details: MNU = N-methyl-N-nitrosourea; tumours at least focally show an inverted (endophytic) papillary growth pattern.

raw_record.support_text: A 100% incidence of thymic lymphomas and gastric carcinomas occurred in rats surviving 14 weeks of intragastric administration of MNU (N-methyl-N-nitrosourea). By the 15th week all animals were either moribund or had succumbed to anoxia caused by pleural effusions from the thymic neoplasia.
raw_record.extra_details: MNU given by intragastric administration; 100% incidence in rats surviving 14 weeks of treatment; tumors (especially thymic) caused anoxia from pleural effusions by week 15.

raw_record.support_text: In the present study, ochratoxin A (OTA) was administered to rats homogenized into feed (oral route) to mimic human exposure, with the dose chosen to produce tumors while avoiding overt nephrotoxicity. A cumulative incidence of animals with a renal tumor of 25% occurred by the 2-year end point, and the development of renal cancer in this study made it a suitable source for studying carcinogenic processes.
raw_record.extra_details: Oral feeding route; dose 300 µg/kg bw initially (until rats reached 333 g) then 100 µg/rat thereafter; 25% cumulative incidence of renal tumors at the 2-year endpoint; treatment well tolerated; this incidence was significantly lower than that in the NTP gavage study at the highest dose.

raw_record.support_text: The BMDL10 for ochratoxin A (OTA) is set at 14.5 µg/kg bw/day based on kidney tumor incidences in rats, providing the carcinogenic reference point used for the Margin of Exposure evaluation.
raw_record.extra_details: BMDL10 of 14.5 µg/kg bw/day derived from kidney tumor incidences in rats.

raw_record.support_text: In two rat long-term studies, acrylamide (AA) in the drinking water increased the incidences of tumors in the mammary gland and thyroid as well as mesotheliomas in the testicular tunic.
raw_record.extra_details: AA administered in the drinking water.

raw_record.support_text: Acrylamide was evaluated for carcinogenicity in two traditional rat bioassays and found to cause several tumor types at oral doses ranging from 0.5 to 3.0 mg/kg/day. The figure legend further refers to 'carcinogenic doses of acrylamide' in micronucleus-induction studies in mice.
raw_record.extra_details: Carcinogenicity evaluated in two traditional rat bioassays; several tumor types at oral doses of 0.5–3.0 mg/kg/day. Acrylamide is also present in the daily diet via the Maillard reaction of asparagine and sugars; its epoxide metabolite glycidamide forms the N7-GA-Gua DNA adduct, a biomarker of exposure. The same compound is described at 'carcinogenic doses' in mouse micronucleus-induction studies.

raw_record.support_text: The most sensitive effects associated with chronic exposures to acrylamide in laboratory animals have been neurotoxicity and an elevation of several tumor types in rats. The USEPA (2007a) established a Reference Dose based on the most sensitive endpoint of nerve damage in rats exposed to acrylamide in drinking water, and established a cancer slope factor (CSF) based on multiple tumor types in rats also exposed via drinking water.
raw_record.extra_details: Chronic exposures in laboratory animals; several/multiple tumor types elevated in rats, no specific tumors named. USEPA (2007a) derived a Reference Dose (RfD) from the most sensitive endpoint of nerve damage and a cancer slope factor (CSF) based on multiple tumor types in rats exposed via drinking water.

raw_record.support_text: Acrylamide administration in drinking water to rats resulted in an increased tumour incidence of breast, thyroid and central nervous system.
raw_record.extra_details: Administration via drinking water (Johnson et al., 1986a, b).

raw_record.support_text: A semi-purified corn-based diet containing 50 mg/kg of pure fumonisin B1 (FB1, purity not <90%), isolated from Fusarium moniliforme strain MRC 826, was fed to 25 rats for up to 26 months. Ten of 15 FB1-treated rats (66%) killed or that died between 18 and 26 months developed primary hepatocellular carcinoma; metastases to heart, lungs or kidneys were present in four of these rats, and no neoplastic changes were seen in any control rat. The authors concluded that FB1 is responsible for the hepatocarcinogenic and hepatotoxic but not all other toxic effects of the culture material in rats.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: primary hepatocellular carcinoma of the liver
raw_record.extra_details: Dietary dose of 50 mg/kg for 26 months; 10/15 (66%) FB1-treated rats killed or dying between 18 and 26 months developed the tumor, with metastases to heart, lungs or kidneys in 4 rats; FB1 purified from F. moniliforme MRC 826 culture material; treated rats also showed micro- and macronodular cirrhosis, cholangiofibrosis nodules at the liver hilus, and chronic interstitial nephritis after 26 months; no lesions in esophagus, heart or forestomach.

raw_record.support_text: Short-term dietary FB₁ (fumonisin B1) induced a high incidence (66%) of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in rats, with metastases to the heart, lungs, or kidneys also observed; earlier initial studies showed a diet containing culture material inoculated with F. moniliforme was carcinogenic in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: 66% incidence of HCC after short-term dietary FB₁; metastases to heart, lungs, or kidneys observed; macronodular cirrhosis and cholangiofibrosis also observed; FB₁ is much less toxic to cultured hepatocytes than AFB₁.

raw_record.support_text: Urothelial carcinogenesis was investigated in rats treated with the carcinogen N-butyl-N-(4-hydroxybutyl) nitrosamine (BHBN) given in the drinking water. With continued BHBN treatment, mucosal hyperplasia progressed to papillary growth and papillary carcinomas developed via papillomas; papillary carcinomas were always induced in rats irrespective of strain or BHBN concentration.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: papillary carcinoma of the urinary bladder
raw_record.extra_details: BHBN given in drinking water; progression through mucosal hyperplasia and papillomas; papillary carcinomas are multifocal but superficial; good model for human papillary bladder carcinoma. Similar findings reported with N-(4-[5-nitro-2-furyl]-2-thiazolyl)formamide and N-methyl-N-nitrosourea.

raw_record.support_text: Oral administration of BBN (N-butyl-N-(4-hydroxybutyl)nitrosamine) produces bladder tumours analogous to those in humans, in a dose- and time-dependent manner. The same passage notes sirolimus had not previously been studied in animal models of bladder cancer, and the study used BBN as the experimental carcinogen to induce bladder tumours (all transitional cell carcinoma) in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Abbreviated BBN; used as an experimental model of bladder carcinogenesis producing tumours analogous to those in humans; induction is dose- and time-dependent; in the study all bladder tumours were TCC (transitional cell carcinoma).

raw_record.support_text: Butyl (4-hydroxybutyl) nitrosamine (BBN) administered to rats at a daily dosage of 20 mg/kg was shown to be a potent specific bladder carcinogen (Druckrey et al., 1964a), with the initial finding confirmed in rats and mice in numerous subsequent studies.
raw_record.extra_details: Daily dosage 20 mg/kg; described as a potent specific (organotropic) bladder carcinogen; finding confirmed in rats and mice.

raw_record.support_text: Oral administration of 4-NQO (4-nitroquinoline 1-oxide) alone (group 1) induced tongue tumors in rats, histopathologically diagnosed as squamous cell papillomas and well-differentiated squamous cell carcinomas. In group 1 (4-NQO alone), the incidence of tongue squamous cell carcinomas was 68.2% (15/22 rats) and of squamous cell papillomas was 13.6% (3/22 rats), with tongue tumors developing at the dorsal site. Dietary FBRA (ferulic-acid-containing rice bran) administration during the initiation or postinitiation phases decreased the incidence and multiplicity of these neoplasms.
raw_record.extra_details: 4-NQO abbreviation; oral administration. Dietary FBRA (ferulic-acid-containing rice bran) at 5-10% given during initiation or postinitiation phases inhibited 4-NQO-induced tongue carcinogenesis; group 2 (5% FBRA, initiation) significantly reduced SCC incidence (p<0.05). FBRA itself was chemopreventive.

raw_record.support_text: Tongue squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) was induced in rats by adding the carcinogen 4-nitroquinoline oxide to drinking water for 19 weeks.
raw_record.extra_details: Agent explicitly designated as a carcinogen and used to induce tongue SCC; administered in drinking water over 19 weeks in a carcinogenicity-induction model.

raw_record.support_text: Laqueur et al. (1963) produced evidence of carcinogenicity of cycasin after long-term feeding of rats with a diet containing 1% to 3% cycad nut flour; within 6-9 months tumors occurred in the kidneys, where the presence of adenomas and undifferentiated tumors was recorded.
raw_record.extra_details: Cycasin was fed via a diet containing 1-3% flour made from cycad nuts; tumors appeared by 6-9 months. In a further experiment Laqueur (1964) fed cycasin at 40, 60, and 100 mg per 100 gm diet or crude cycad meal at 2.5% to weanling and young adult rats; of 34 survivors autopsied beyond 8 months, 32 had renal tumors.

raw_record.support_text: The first evidence of the carcinogenic effect of Cycasin was obtained by Laqueur et al. after feeding Cycas meal to rats, who observed mainly malignant liver and kidney tumors. These findings were later confirmed and extended by the same group and many other authors, with oral administration of pure Cycasin or Cycas meal producing malignancies in mouse, rat, hamster, guinea pig and the fish Brachydanio rerio, including malignant liver and kidney tumors.
raw_record.extra_details: First reported after feeding Cycas meal; confirmed with pure Cycasin and Cycas meal. Cycasin is an azoxyglucoside isolated from Cycas revoluta.

raw_record.support_text: Histological types of most tumors in rats induced by cycasin (or MAM) were: liver — liver cell adenoma, liver cell carcinoma, bile duct adenoma, and cystadenoma; kidney — adenoma, interstitial tumor, nephroblastoma, and sarcoma; intestine — adenoma and adenocarcinoma.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: liver cell adenoma, liver cell carcinoma, bile duct adenoma, cystadenoma
raw_record.extra_details: Tumors induced in rats by cycasin or its aglycone MAM; single administration also induced tumors of kidney and large intestine in rats (MAM aglycone is methylazoxymethanol).

raw_record.support_text: Among the rats exposed only to DEN (N-nitrosodiethylamine), 71% presented esophageal neoplastic lesions and 73% hepatic lesions. The paper treats DEN as a carcinogen whose ingested dose corresponds to esophageal neoplasia incidence and whose doses are described as known to be carcinogenic.
raw_record.extra_details: DEN administered in drinking water at ~2.9 mg/kg/day; 71% of DEN-only rats developed esophageal neoplasia. DEN is referred to as 'the carcinogen' and as having 'doses known to be carcinogenic'.

raw_record.support_text: Rats in Group III were induced with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) by providing 0.01% DEN (diethylnitrosamine) through drinking water for 16 weeks, attributing liver tumor induction to DEN exposure by the oral route. Group IV received Shorea robusta bark extract (SRBE) before and during DEN administration in a chemoprevention protocol.
raw_record.extra_details: DEN was given at 0.01% in drinking water for 16 weeks to induce HCC in rats (Group III). The study investigates the protective effect of Shorea robusta bark extract (SRBE, 500 mg/kg body weight) against DEN-induced hepatocarcinogenesis.

raw_record.support_text: Administration of diethylnitrosamine (DEN) solution in drinking water to experimental animals induced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Tumor burden (sum of visible tumor nodule volumes) was significantly higher than in the control group, and glutathione S-transferase placental form (GST-P)-positive foci characteristic of hepatocarcinogenesis were induced by DEN. Gross examination showed that tumors were found only in the livers of groups A and B animals, were absent in control and classical groups, and tumorigenesis rates reached 100% in groups A and B by week 9-12 of DEN feeding.
raw_record.extra_details: DEN given in drinking water using a body-weight-based protocol for 6 (group A) or 9 (group B) consecutive weeks; 100% tumorigenesis by weeks 9-12; tumors confined to liver; GST-P(+) dysplastic nodule staining increased from week 4 in groups A and B. A classical constant 100 ppm DEN group given for 9 weeks and controls given regular water showed no gross liver tumors at week 12. HCC induction was accompanied by liver cirrhosis only in group B. Also known as N-nitrosodiethylamine (DEN).

raw_record.support_text: Rats continuously exposed to diethylnitrosamine at 50 ppm in the drinking water were bled weekly. Three animals (XI 180, XII 40, XII 32) developed detectable serum AFP levels after 8, 12, and 16 weeks of continuous carcinogen administration, and their livers contained hemorrhagic and yellow nodules. Histologic examination revealed moderately to well differentiated hepatocellular carcinomas in each animal.
raw_record.extra_details: Administered continuously at 50 ppm in drinking water; rats also developed elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels detectable by agar double diffusion after 8-16 weeks.

raw_record.support_text: In rats, orally administered furan also dose-dependently induces mononuclear leukemia.
raw_record.extra_details: Dose-dependent induction following oral administration.

raw_record.support_text: In NTP 1993 studies, furan administered by gavage in corn oil induced hepatocellular tumors in rats, consistent with the paper's statement that the liver is the main target organ of furan-induced toxicity and carcinogenicity in rodents.
raw_record.extra_details: NTP 1993 study; administered by gavage in corn oil.

raw_record.support_text: Furan is a carcinogen in rodents; carcinogenicity studies in rodents showed the occurrence of cholangiocarcinomas in rats (Moser et al. 2009; NTP 1993; Von Tungeln et al. 2017).
raw_record.extra_details: Cholangiocarcinomas occurred in rats per Moser et al. 2009; NTP 1993; Von Tungeln et al. 2017.

raw_record.support_text: Of 15 rats fed nafenopin, 3 developed pancreatic tumors between 20 and 22 months; the other 2 had solitary acinar cell adenomas of the pancreas.
The studies of nafenopin, including the long-term rat bioassay of Reddy and Rao, were described as providing sufficient evidence for the carcinogenicity of nafenopin in experimental animals.
raw_record.extra_details: Sufficient-evidence conclusion for carcinogenicity in experimental animals.

raw_record.support_text: In 1967, Sugimura and Fujimura produced adenocarcinoma in the glandular stomach of rats by oral administration of N-methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine (MNNG). When given in drinking water, this compound induced both benign and malignant neoplasms of the stomach strikingly similar to gastric tumors in man, and MNNG has been described as a most reliable carcinogen for investigation of gastric neoplasia.
raw_record.extra_details: MNNG given in drinking water induced both benign and malignant stomach neoplasms resembling human gastric tumors; described as a most reliable carcinogen for gastric neoplasia research.

raw_record.support_text: In a rat gastric cancer model induced by MNNG (N-methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine), 90 animals were treated with MNNG while 10 served as controls. All control animals were negative, whereas 62 of the 90 MNNG-treated animals showed positive ultrasound results for gastric tumor. Pathologic evaluation confirmed cancerous alterations in the MNNG-treated rats, including poorly differentiated carcinoma, with no pathologic changes in controls, establishing MNNG as an agent that induces gastric tumors in this rat model.
raw_record.extra_details: MNNG used as a gastric cancer-inducing agent; ultrasound (BMUI) screening yielded 62 positive/28 negative among 90 treated animals, with 57 pathologically positive cases; poorly differentiated cancerous alterations were found; no evidence of metastasis or invasion at necropsy; hyperplasia was not included in gastric cancer classification. Aliases: MNNG.

raw_record.support_text: Experiments on 170 rats given N-methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine (MNNG) in drinking water at 167 mg/l were studied for the genesis of experimental stomach cancer. The paper describes the process of carcinogenesis and states malignization of epithelial complexes developed, showing that MNNG administered orally induced stomach cancer in these rats.
raw_record.extra_details: MNNG administered in drinking water at 167 mg/l; 170 rats; stomach carcinogenesis focused on the glandular stomach, which is analogous to the human stomach. Paper also notes the blastomogenic (tumor-inducing) effect of MNNG on the gastrointestinal tract of rodents, canines, and other animals, with varying evaluation among authors (e.g., Sugimura and Kowachi 1973).

raw_record.support_text: The paper states that Sugimura's group was further able to induce adenocarcinomas in the glandular stomach of rats by administering the carcinogen N-Methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine (NG) orally in drinking water (Sugimura and Fujimura 1967).
raw_record.extra_details: NG referred to as 'this carcinogen'; administered in drinking water; attributed to Sugimura and Fujimura (1967).

raw_record.support_text: Retrorsine (fig. 6) is also carcinogenic and produces a variety of tumours in rats when it is administered orally (IARC, 1976). Retrorsine is one of the main alkaloids present in the Senecio plant species.
raw_record.extra_details: Reported as carcinogenic with reference to IARC, 1976; named as one of the main alkaloids present in the Senecio plant species. Administered orally.

raw_record.support_text: Oral administration of retrorsine produced tumors primarily in the liver of rats; retrorsine is among the over 20 pyrrolizidine alkaloids established to be carcinogenic in experimental animals.
Several pyrrolizidine alkaloids were shown to be carcinogenic in the rat: liver tumors developed in 4/10 males and 0/4 females fed retrorsine.
raw_record.extra_details: Pyrrolizidine alkaloid; liver tumors in 4/10 male and 0/4 female rats fed the compound.

raw_record.support_text: NDEOL (N-nitrosodiethanolamine) treatment induced liver tumors in rats; an approximately 50-fold increase in the daily dose level was necessary to halve the median tumor induction time. Tumor induction times were much longer even at the highest dose levels and the carcinogenic response was considerably less affected by changes in dose compared to 4-DAB. Liver tumor data for NDEOL were taken from the literature.
raw_record.extra_details: Alias NDEOL. Carcinogenic response considerably less affected by changes in dose than 4-DAB; ~50-fold increase in daily dose needed to halve median tumor induction time.

raw_record.support_text: The carcinogenicity of NDELA (N-nitrosodiethanolamine) was extensively studied in rats, mice, and hamsters. After oral administration, NDELA induced primarily liver tumors in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: NDELA (compound 6, Figure 1) is an environmentally prevalent N-nitrosamine found in cosmetics, food products, synthetic cutting fluids, and tobacco/tobacco smoke.

raw_record.support_text: Continuous feeding of rats with 3-methylcholanthrene induced palpable mammary tumors as early as the 20th day from the start of the feeding.
raw_record.extra_details: Palpable tumors appeared as early as day 20 of feeding.

raw_record.support_text: All 85 rats fed 3-methylcholanthrene (3-MCA) developed mammary tumours in the period from one week before to 43 weeks after the last dose of 3-MCA. In 81 of the rats the tumours were adenomata, typical in their histological appearance of adenomata induced by this carcinogen in earlier experiments; the other 4 rats developed fibro-adenomata, which were disregarded in this study.
raw_record.extra_details: Dietary feeding of the carcinogen; 199 palpable adenomata in total across 81 rats; 4 rats developed fibroadenomata which were excluded from the study. Follow-up experiments examined the effect of adrenalectomy and ovariectomy on the induced tumours.

raw_record.support_text: Table 2 reports target organs of carcinogenicity and TD50 values for heterocyclic amines from lifetime dietary feeding studies. IQ produced tumors of the liver, intestine, Zymbal gland, clitoral gland and skin in rats with a TD50 of 0.7 mg/kg b.w./day.
raw_record.extra_details: 2-Amino-3-methylimidazo[4,5-f]quinoline; TD50 0.7 mg/kg b.w./day; lifetime feeding.

raw_record.support_text: Among the heterocyclic amines, 2-amino-3-methylimidazo[4,5-f]quinoline (IQ) has been shown to induce colon tumors in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Also called IQ; heterocyclic amine in cooked foods; induced 11 colon tumors in F344 rats in this study; humans exposed to ~0.2 ug/d.

raw_record.support_text: The peroxisome proliferator methylclofenapate has been shown to induce Leydig cell tumors (LCTs) in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Listed among several peroxisome proliferators shown to induce LCTs in rats (Tucker and Orton, 1995).

raw_record.support_text: Photomicrograph of well-differentiated hepatocellular carcinoma induced by methyl clofenapate in rat liver. The tumor cells contain prominent nucleoli.
raw_record.extra_details: Tumor cells contained prominent nucleoli; tumors were also capable of metastasizing to the lung and were transplanted successfully in syngeneic hosts.

raw_record.support_text: The peroxisome proliferator clofibrate has been shown to induce Leydig cell tumors (LCTs) in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Listed among several peroxisome proliferators shown to induce LCTs in rats (Tucker and Orton, 1995).

raw_record.support_text: KE #5 (Hepatic Tumors) supporting data state that clofibrate causes liver tumor formation after longer term exposure in rats (Reddy and Qureshi, 1979; Svoboda and Arzarnoff, 1979). The paper concludes that the confidence that clofibrate operates via a PPARα MOA to induce liver tumors in rodents is very high, establishing that clofibrate induces rodent liver tumors.
raw_record.extra_details: Induction of rodent liver tumors occurs via a PPARα-mediated (non-genotoxic) mode of action; the mutagenic MOA was scored as very low confidence, with high confidence that the rodent liver tumor induction is not caused by a mutagenic MOA, supported by extensive negative DNA interaction/damage data.

raw_record.support_text: The paper describes 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) as a carcinogen and reports that the tight junctions of DMH-induced rat colon tumors are leakier than normal colon. Treatment of rats with the carcinogen DMH induced a progressive increase in aberrant colonic crypts (a putative pre-neoplastic colonic phenotype) and increased colon epithelial TJ permeability prior to the development of tumors.
raw_record.extra_details: DMH is explicitly called 'the carcinogen DMH'. Treatment induced a progressive increase in the number of aberrant colonic crypts (putative pre-neoplastic phenotype) and increased tight junction permeability of the colon epithelium prior to tumor development; tumors were contrasted with normal colon TJ permeability.

raw_record.support_text: In the dietary fiber intervention study, colorectal tumors were induced in rats by the carcinogen 1,2-dimethylhydrazine. The induction of tumor formation by 1,2-dimethylhydrazine was enhanced in guar-gum-fed (GG12) rats, with the neoplasms remaining at the adenoma stage, while in the crystalline-cellulose-fed (C8G4) group the initiation step was depressed, resulting in fewer tumors. The tumors scored were colorectal adenomas and adenocarcinomas.
raw_record.extra_details: 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) was used as the colorectal carcinogen in a rat model (1,2-dimethylhydrazine-induced rat colorectal tumor model); dietary fiber feeding (guar gum, crystalline cellulose) modulated the tumor yield (tumor development was enhanced in GG12 rats while initiation appeared depressed in C8G4 rats).

raw_record.support_text: Tumorigenesis in the rat small intestine has been induced by 1,2-dimethylhydrazine [131-134]. This is reported among factors and agents that induce tumor formation in the small intestine.
raw_record.extra_details: Reported induction of tumorigenesis in the rat small intestine; supported by references [131-134]. The other agents mentioned in the same paragraph (aromatic amines, benzo[a]pyrene, aflatoxin B1, cyclophosphamide, Trp-P-1, Trp-P-2) are described only in terms of metabolic activation in intestinal tissue preparations, which is outside the carcinogenicity claim scope.

raw_record.support_text: The authors state that 1,2-dimethylhydrazine produces intestinal tumors in rats similar to intestinal tumors in humans (Druckrey, 1970), and venture the opinion that it acts by prolonging the half-life of stem cells or their immediate descendants, preventing their regular differentiation and shedding.
raw_record.extra_details: Compared to intestinal tumors in humans; proposed mechanism is prolongation of stem-cell half-life preventing differentiation.

raw_record.support_text: Colon tumors were induced in rats by treatment with 1,2-dimethylhydrazine, and the induced tumorous tissue and adjacent grossly normal tissue were compared using morphological, histochemical and immunohistochemical analyses.
raw_record.extra_details: Used as a chemical inducing agent in a chemically-induced colon cancer rat model in which tumorous and adjacent grossly-normal tissues were studied morphologically, histochemically and immunohistochemically; index of tissue damage was significantly different from normal untreated colon.

raw_record.support_text: MNU, 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) and azoxymethane (AOM) were used as carcinogens in models of colon carcinogenesis. Around one-third of the colonic carcinomas induced by DMH had mutated K-ras oncogene.
raw_record.extra_details: Explicitly described as a carcinogen (DMH); induced colonic carcinomas, about one-third of which carried mutated K-ras.

raw_record.support_text: The carcinogen 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) induces colon tumors in the rat. The rat colon tumors contain β-catenin mutations in the glycogen synthase kinase-3β consensus region, with the majority clustering around Ser33, a pattern differing from human colon cancers.
raw_record.extra_details: Also known as DMH. Rat colon tumors contain β-catenin mutations clustered around Ser33, distinct from the human colon cancer pattern.

raw_record.support_text: Polyphenols derived from red wine reduced colon tumour yield and oxidative DNA damage induced in rat colon mucosa by the model carcinogen 1,2-dimethylhydrazine.
raw_record.extra_details: Described as a 'model carcinogen'; induced colon tumour yield and oxidative DNA damage in rat colon mucosa. Note: this is the inducer/tumor-induction agent in a study of red wine polyphenol chemoprevention.

raw_record.support_text: The effects of Diabenol on colon carcinogenesis induced by 1,2-dimethylhydrazine in rats were studied; the carcinogen caused colon tumors, and Diabenol inhibited the multiplicity of all colon tumors and the incidence of carcinomas in the ascending colon.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: colon tumors (including carcinomas of the ascending colon)
raw_record.extra_details: Used as the inducing carcinogen in a colon carcinogenesis model; Diabenol treatment reduced tumor multiplicity and carcinoma incidence in the ascending colon.

raw_record.support_text: Experiments in colon cancer showed that 20% cellulose content decreased tumor incidence caused by 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) to 33%, compared with 92% of tumors developed in animals fed a fiber-free diet, i.e., DMH induced colon tumors in rats. Corncob fiber (15%) treated with the fungus Pleurotus os. had a significant protective effect against DMH-induced rat colon cancer.
raw_record.extra_details: DMH used as chemically-induced colon cancer model; tumor incidence 92% in animals fed a fiber-free diet, reduced to 33% with a 20% cellulose diet; corncob fiber (15%) treated with Pleurotus ostreatus protected against DMH-induced rat colon cancer. Aliases: DMH.

raw_record.support_text: 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH), a potent procarcinogen with selectivity for colon, can produce colon cancer in experimental rats. Experimental colon cancer induced by DMH in rats mimics human colon cancer and is therefore used as an ideal model for chemoprevention studies.
raw_record.extra_details: Described as a potent procarcinogen with selectivity for the colon; used experimentally to induce colon cancer in rats as a model that mimics human colon cancer.

raw_record.support_text: 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) was used to establish a rat colon carcinogenesis model; DMH-induced rats showed significantly higher expression of cyclin D1 in carcinogenic colon tissues relative to normal colonic tissues, indicating DMH administration induced colon carcinogenesis in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: DMH is a chemical carcinogen used to induce colon carcinogenesis in the rat model; carcinogenic rats also showed elevated cyclin D1 expression.

raw_record.support_text: The study investigated the effect of the maleimide-derived protein kinase inhibitor MI-1 on blood cells under conditions of 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH)-induced colon carcinogenesis in rats, establishing DMH as the carcinogen used to induce colon tumors. In paragraph 5 the paper states that all rats that received DMH were found to have colon tumors.
raw_record.extra_details: DMH (1,2-dimethylhydrazine) was used as the chemical inducer in a colon carcinogenesis model in rats; all DMH-treated rats developed colonic tumors. MI-1 was tested as an inhibitor of DMH-induced carcinogenesis, not as a carcinogen.

raw_record.support_text: In animal experiments, a few doses of dimethylhydrazine (DMH) can induce multicentric colon tumors in a short period of time (cites 102, 148). Total dietary fat appears to augment tumorigenesis by DMH in the rat. DMH is referred to as a colon carcinogen in this context.
raw_record.extra_details: A few doses suffice to induce tumors in a short period of time; passage refers to DMH among colon carcinogens.

raw_record.support_text: The study assessed effects of probiotics during 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) induced colon carcinogenesis in rats. Rats were treated with DMH for a period of 16 weeks; DMH treatment resulted in a statistically significant increase in total sialic acid and COX-2 expression and induced tumor incidence, tumor multiplicity, and average tumor size, establishing DMH as the colon-carcinogen inducer in the rat model.
raw_record.extra_details: DMH (1,2-dimethylhydrazine, alias N,N-dimethyldiazene) used as the chemical colon-carcinogen inducer in rats at 16 weeks of treatment; probiotics Lactobacillus plantarum AdF10 and Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG reduced tumor incidence, multiplicity, tumor size, and COX-2 expression.

raw_record.support_text: 1,2-Dimethylhydrazine (DMH) is described as a potential carcinogen that acts as a DNA alkylating agent, and administration of DMH induced colon cancer in rats, with an increase in the activity of CYP2E1 and reduction of phase II enzyme activities.
raw_record.extra_details: Described as a potential carcinogen acting as a DNA alkylating agent; DMH administration raised CYP2E1 activity and lowered phase II enzyme activities; troxerutin supplementation reversed the pathological changes.

raw_record.support_text: Colon cancer was induced chemically (DMH, 1,2-dimethylhydrazine) in rats according to a modified standardised protocol, and after 16 weeks of DMH treatment the rats developed colon tumours with 85% tumour incidence, tumour multiplicity of 2.87 ± 0.64 and average tumour volume of 2.04 cm³. Histopathological analysis of DMH-treated rat colon sections showed well-differentiated neoplasia with moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. The model was validated biochemically (elevated serum TSA, p53, COX-2, VEGF, CEA) and histologically against human colorectal carcinoma.
raw_record.extra_details: DMH used as chemical inducer of colon cancer in rats (modified protocol of Chadha et al. 2011); at 16 weeks tumour incidence 85 ± 5.0%, tumour multiplicity 2.87 ± 0.64, average tumour volume 2.04 ± 0.04 cm³; model compared histologically and biochemically (TSA, mutated p53, COX-2, VEGF, CEA) to human colorectal carcinoma. Alias: DMH.

raw_record.support_text: Colon carcinogenesis in rats can be induced by 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH). DMH treatment causes intracellular alkalosis due to a significant increase in Na+/H+ exchanger-mediated H+ efflux.
raw_record.extra_details: DMH (1,2-dimethylhydrazine) treatment causes intracellular alkalosis due to a significant increase in Na+/H+ exchanger-mediated H+ efflux (Kanwar et al. 2009).

raw_record.support_text: In a rat colorectal carcinogenesis model, 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) induced tumors: the DMH-treated group exhibited a 100% tumor incidence with 2.5 tumors/polyps per tumor-bearing rat, whereas the normal control group had no tumors.
raw_record.extra_details: DMH used as the inducing carcinogen in a study of the chemopreventive agent boeravinone B (BB); DMH group showed 100% tumor incidence and 25 tumors/polyps across 10 rats. DMH-induced rats also showed elevated LPO and reduced CAT, GSH, and SOD, and increased cytochrome P450 and cytochrome B5 with reduced glutathione reductase.

raw_record.support_text: Gallic acid was able to reduce the severity of dimethylhydrazine-induced oxidative stress in rats, thereby preventing the induction of colon carcinoma by this compound, which the text explicitly refers to as a carcinogenic compound.
raw_record.extra_details: The compound is labeled carcinogenic; its carcinogenic effect involves induction of oxidative stress that gallic acid mitigated. No exposure route, dose, or strain details reported.

raw_record.support_text: 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (1,2-DMH) is described as a widely used agent for developing colorectal cancer (CRC) in rodents. DMH-induced CRC in rats is used as a model for studying the molecular events of CRC, with rat models exhibiting an adenoma-carcinoma sequence like that found in humans.
raw_record.extra_details: Also referred to as 1,2-DMH and DMH. Used as an experimental model agent to induce CRC in rodents for studying tumor biology and molecular events; the paper notes DMH-induced CRC in rats does not represent the full complexity of the human disease.

raw_record.support_text: In the DMH-treated control groups, dimethylhydrazine (DMH) induction produced colon tumors in 25/26 rats on regular chow and 27/28 rats on placebo beadlets, with colon cancers in 21/26 and 27/28 animals respectively, demonstrating that DMH induces colonic neoplasms in this rat model.
raw_record.extra_details: DMH used as the inducing carcinogen in a chemoprevention model; tumor counts per animal (colon tumors 2.08 and 3.21 in the two control groups).

raw_record.support_text: 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) was used to induce the rat colon cancer model, in which the combination of curcumin and catechins significantly lowered the incidence of colon tumors compared with individual and control group rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Abbreviation DMH; DMH-induced rat colon cancer model, reported in the Table 1 entry as 'DMH-induced rat colon cancer' with ACF number and colon tumor incidence decreased 57% and 53% in the combination treatment group.

raw_record.support_text: The passage discusses DMH (1,2-dimethylhydrazine) induction of colon carcinomas in rats, as an established experimental model of intestinal carcinogenesis, and notes that additional administration of immunodepressants and immunostimulators had no effect on DMH induction of colon carcinomas.
raw_record.extra_details: DMH (also rendered DMH in text) induces colon carcinoma in intact rats; this induction is the basis of the reviewed experimental colon carcinogenesis model. Abbreviation ambiguity in the entity list resolved to 1,2-dimethylhydrazine based on the azoxymethane/DMH colon-carcinoma context.

raw_record.support_text: Dimethylhydrazine is described as one of the highly efficient intestinal carcinogens in the rat.
raw_record.extra_details: Reported alongside azoxymethane and methylazoxymethanol; cholestyramine (2% diet) strikingly enhanced its carcinogenic effect, especially in the large intestine.

raw_record.support_text: Rats were treated with the carcinogen 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH). In DMH-treated rats, the incidence of intestinal tumor formation ranged from 52% (Group C) to 83% (Group D), with colonic tumor incidence up to 23/29 depending on diet. Histologic evaluation showed both polypoid adenomas and well-differentiated and mucinous carcinomas of the colon, plus small-intestine adenocarcinomas, and some tumors metastasized to abdominal organs, lungs, and pericardium.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: intestinal (gastrointestinal and colonic) tumors, including colonic adenomas and well-differentiated and mucinous carcinomas and small-intestine adenocarcinomas
raw_record.extra_details: Diets containing bile salts (Groups B, D) increased colon tumor number per tumor-bearing rat, tumor size, and distal (anal-ward) shift of tumors relative to other groups. DMH given as an inducing carcinogen; subcutaneous administration implied but not stated.

raw_record.support_text: In the colon carcinogenesis model using 1,2-DMH (1,2-dimethylhydrazine), 87-89% of histologically examined colonic tumors in 1,2-DMH-treated rats were adenocarcinomas, 29-52% of which had metastasized, and 84-96% showed infiltrative growth. Adenomas progressed into adenocarcinomas, and tumor growth was aggressively infiltrative with metastases in lungs, pleura, liver, and abdominal lymph nodes.
raw_record.extra_details: Alias 1,2-DMH. Colonic tumors seen in 20/69 (29%) animals after three courses of laparotomy between days 152 and 251. Autochthonous colonic tumor model; adenocarcinomas showed infiltrative growth and metastasized.

raw_record.support_text: Tumors of the colon were induced in rats by the administration of 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH), and the rats developed DMH-induced colonic adenocarcinomas. The colonic tumors from DMH-treated animals were used to study inhibition of protein synthesis by sodium cyanate.
raw_record.extra_details: DMH administered to rats and reported to induce colon tumors/colonic adenocarcinomas used in the cyanate protein-synthesis inhibition study; route of DMH administration not stated.

raw_record.support_text: In the study, colon adenocarcinomas were induced by 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) treatment in rats, and the paper states that 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) induced colorectal tumours in rodents, which display many histological features in common with human colonic adenocarcinomas.
raw_record.extra_details: Abbreviation DMH; 1,2-dimethylhydrazine-induced colorectal tumours in rodents display many histological features in common with human colonic adenocarcinomas; agent used as the experimental inducer of colon adenocarcinoma for evaluating A/H blood-group and CD44/CD44v6 antigen expression.

raw_record.support_text: Acrylonitrile (AN) is a multisite tumorigen in rats, most notably producing tumors in the brain. The carcinogenicity of AN has been evaluated in 10 separate rat studies, which have shown the brain as the primary target organ.
raw_record.extra_details: Described as a multisite tumorigen in rats with brain as the primary target organ; based on 10 separate rat bioassays.

raw_record.support_text: Acrylonitrile, an important industrial chemical as well as a tobacco smoke constituent, induces tumors at multiple sites in rats, including forestomach, central nervous system, and mammary gland.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: forestomach, central nervous system, and mammary gland tumors
raw_record.extra_details: Acrylonitrile is an important industrial chemical and a tobacco smoke constituent; inducing tumors at multiple sites in rats.

raw_record.support_text: Benzo[a]pyrene and dibenzo[a,l]pyrene, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons found in occupational, environmental, and dietary sources, successfully induced mammary tumors in the rat.
raw_record.extra_details: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon found in occupational (industrial combustion), environmental (cigarette smoke), and dietary (broiled food) sources.

raw_record.support_text: Wang found that saline extracts from rat sarcomas that had been induced with the carcinogen 3,4-benzpyrene produce a typical delayed hypersensitivity reaction when injected into rats immunized against such tumours. This indicates that 3,4-benzpyrene induced sarcomas in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Chemically-induced rat sarcomas used to study tumour-specific transplantation-type antigens and oncofoetal antigens; called 'the carcinogen 3,4-benzpyrene' in the passage.

raw_record.support_text: Ethylnitrosourea induces breast tumors — fibroadenomas (FA) as well as low and high grade infiltrating ductal carcinomas (IDC) — in the rat. This system was used to evaluate the pharmacokinetic characteristics of Gd-DTPA, Gadomer-17, and albumin-Gd-DTPA by Dynamic Contrast Enhanced MRI to differentiate the different tumor types.
raw_record.cancer_or_tumor: breast tumors, comprising fibroadenomas (benign) and low and high grade infiltrating ductal carcinomas (malignant)
raw_record.extra_details: Ethylnitrosourea was used as a tumor-induction system to compare the MRI pharmacokinetic enhancing characteristics of the contrast agents Gd-DTPA (<1 kD), Gadomer-17 (35 kD), and albumin-Gd-DTPA (70–90 kD).

raw_record.support_text: N-Ethyl-N-nitrosourea (ENU), similar to MNU, is a potent carcinogen inducing mainly tumors of nervous system and forming N7-ethyl-guanine and O6-ethyl-guanine adducts. The brain is described as the target tissue of MNU and ENU tumorigenesis in rats, where O6-guanine adducts remain relatively persistent because of repair deficiency compared with repair-proficient liver.
raw_record.extra_details: Also called ENU. Described as a potent carcinogen.

raw_record.support_text: Spontaneous mammary gland cancers in rats, generally adenocarcinomas, can be enhanced with treatment with genotoxic carcinogens like DMBA, N-nitrosomethylurea, and N-ethyl-N-nitrosourea (ENU). These induced mammary tumors are hormone-dependent and can be modulated by reproductive status, hormone treatment, diet, and the dose and timing of carcinogen administration.
raw_record.extra_details: Referred to as ENU in text; called a genotoxic carcinogen; enhances spontaneous rat mammary gland cancers. Induced tumors are hormone-dependent and modulated by reproductive status, hormone treatment, diet, and dose/timing (Davis and Fenton 2013).

raw_record.support_text: The paper cites previous examples of glial cell tumor lines that were initiated from rat brain tumors which had been induced by ethylnitrosourea, indicating that ethylnitrosourea induced brain tumors in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Tumor lines derived from these ethylnitrosourea-induced rat brain tumors showed skeletal muscle differentiation (reported as prior findings, refs. 16 and 17).

raw_record.support_text: This study shows that NNK induces large tumours in the lung of rats, and that the nitrosoamines have a greater effect on the lung when compared to the exocrine pancreas.
raw_record.extra_details: NNK is 4-(methylnitrosamino)-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanone. The nitrosoamines showed a greater effect on the lung than the exocrine pancreas.

raw_record.support_text: The paper states that 4-(Methylnitrosamino)-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanone (NNK) and its metabolite 4-(Methylnitrosamino)-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanol (NNAL) are both potent pulmonary carcinogens in rats. The study treated male F344 rats with 10 ppm of NNK, (R)-NNAL, or (S)-NNAL in drinking water and quantified POB-DNA adducts, supporting that lung carcinogenesis by NNK and NNAL involves retention of (S)-NNAL and reconversion to NNK.
raw_record.extra_details: Tobacco-specific nitrosamine found only in tobacco products and their smoke; described as a potent pulmonary carcinogen in rats.

raw_record.support_text: NNK induces tumors of the pancreas in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: A tobacco-specific nitrosamine; coexists with NNN in tobacco products.

raw_record.support_text: The tobacco smoke-specific nicotine-derived nitrosaminoketone 4-(methylnitrosamino)-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanone is described as highly specific in causing bronchogenic cancer in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: A tobacco-specific N-nitrosamine formed from alkaloids and nitro compounds; listed in Table with 'Sufficient' evidence in lab animals.

raw_record.support_text: An early-stage lung cancer model was induced in rats by NNK (4-(N-nitrosomethyl)-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanone). Ninety-five weeks after NNK treatment, a lung adenocarcinoma was detected at histopathological examination, and fourteen lung tumors were found in the NNK treatment group but none in the control group. The incidence of lung cancer was significantly higher in the NNK group than in the control group (100% vs 0%, P<0.01), showing that NNK can induce early-stage lung carcinogenesis in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: NNK is the abbreviation used in the paper. Lung tumor incidence 100% in NNK group vs 0% in control at 95 weeks after treatment; 14 lung tumors total in the treatment group; no lung tumor detected at week 20. Model described as an early-stage lung carcinogenesis model.

raw_record.support_text: The text notes coherence with carcinogenicity studies of NNN and NNK in rats, in which NNN induces predominantly esophageal and oral cavity cancer, but not lung cancer.
raw_record.extra_details: NNN = N'-nitrosonornicotine; induces predominantly esophageal and oral cavity cancer, but not lung cancer, in rats.

raw_record.support_text: NNK (N-Methyl-N-nitrosamino-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanone), a tobacco-specific nitrosamine, causes tumors in the nasal cavity, lung, and liver of rats (Hoffmann et al., 1984), with no evident dose-response relationship for lung tumors between 5 and 50 mg/kg NNK.
raw_record.extra_details: Tobacco-specific nitrosamine; no dose-response evident for lung tumors between 5 and 50 mg/kg NNK; O6-methylguanine adduct dose-response in rat lung described as supralinear.

raw_record.support_text: Analysis of smokers' urine confirmed NNK uptake in amounts similar to those estimated from NNK levels in cigarette smoke, resulting in total doses approximately equivalent to the lowest total doses of NNK that can induce lung tumors in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: NNK = 4-(N-nitrosomethylamino)-1-[3-pyridyl]butan-1-one, a tobacco-specific nitrosamine. Oral-dose threshold referenced from prior carcinogenicity studies; doses in smokers approximate the lowest tumor-inducing dose in rats.

raw_record.support_text: Benzidine gave rise to colonic adenocarcinomas in rats, with the incidence of colon tumors higher in males than in females.
raw_record.extra_details: Colon tumor incidence was higher in males than in females (females tended to die of breast cancer). Ref 255.

raw_record.support_text: Research on the suspected bladder carcinogen benzidine led to demonstration of its carcinogenic properties in rats, inducing tumours of the rectum, sebaceous ear glands, and liver. Bladder tumours had not been induced in rats, only in one dog.
raw_record.extra_details: Tumours of rectum in rats; earlier suspicion (shared with the bladder carcinogen question) had been amply confirmed.

raw_record.support_text: Estradiol was shown to be carcinogenic in rats, giving rise to mammary tumors; this literature was reviewed by Shimkin, Gardner et al., and Bischoff.
raw_record.extra_details: Interest in steroid estrogen carcinogenicity was aroused by the apparent success of ablation therapy in breast cancer; many human and animal breast tumors are estrogen-dependent.

raw_record.support_text: In rats, estradiol (E₂) treatment for 6 months induced bona fide mammary gland tumors (MGTs); these E₂-induced MGTs (n = 6) showed elevated cyclin D1 (24.8-fold), cyclin D3 (9-fold) and cdk4 (3-fold) expression relative to age-matched untreated controls. The work is framed as E₂-induced mammary oncogenesis in the rat.
raw_record.extra_details: Alias: E₂. E₂-induced mammary oncogenesis; MGTs observed after 6 months of estradiol treatment and used to measure cyclin D1, cyclin D3 and cdk4 protein expression (24.8-, 9- and 3-fold increases, respectively).

raw_record.support_text: COX-2 protein has been detected in rat mammary tumours induced by various carcinogens, including N-nitrosomethyl urea (NMU). Based on immunohistochemical analyses, COX-2 protein was observed in the epithelial cells within the mammary tumours.
raw_record.extra_details: Listed among 'various carcinogens' that induced rat mammary tumours; COX-2 protein detected within the epithelial cells of these tumours.

raw_record.support_text: More than 80% of mammary tumors induced by the alkylating agent N-nitrosomethylurea (NMU) contain activating Ha-ras-1 mutations, with G→A transitions in the second base of codon 12. NMU induces rat mammary tumors/carcinomas.
raw_record.extra_details: NMU (N-nitrosomethylurea) described as an alkylating agent; >80% of NMU-induced mammary tumors contain activating Ha-ras-1 mutations as G→A transitions in the second base of codon 12.

raw_record.support_text: The significance of O6-alkylguanine has been clearly demonstrated in carcinogenesis experiments involving the induction of mammary tumours in rats with N-nitrosomethylurea (NMU). A high proportion of NMU-induced mammary tumours contain Ha-ras oncogenes activated by G-A transitions at the 12th codon.
raw_record.extra_details: Induction attributed to O6-methylguanine mispairing with thymine during DNA replication; a high proportion of NMU-induced mammary tumours contain Ha-ras oncogenes activated by G-A transitions at the 12th codon.

raw_record.support_text: The glioma C6 cell line was cloned from a rat glial tumor induced by N-nitrosomethylurea, indicating that N-nitrosomethylurea induced this glial neoplasm in a rat.
raw_record.extra_details: The C6 cell line was subsequently cloned from the N-nitrosomethylurea-induced rat glial tumor (rat glial tumor induced by N-nitrosomethylurea [22]).

raw_record.support_text: The paper refers to nitrosomethylurea as a well-known carcinogen that specifically causes point mutations in which guanine is replaced by adenine. When administered to rats, nitrosomethylurea causes breast cancer in which H-ras-1 is activated, activation being the consequence of a change from guanine-guanine-adenine to guanine-adenine-adenine in the 12th codon.
