raw_record.extra_details: Also referred to as a 'well-known carcinogen'; activates H-ras-1 through a G to A point mutation in codon 12 (GGA to GAA).

raw_record.support_text: Nitrosomethylurea (N-nitrosomethylurea) is described as inducing rat mammary tumours in a majority (>80%) of cases, associated with a point mutation of the H-ras gene at the twelfth codon, attributed to formation of O6-methylguanine and a GC to AT transition.
raw_record.extra_details: Also called nitrosomethylurea (NMU). Induction of rat mammary tumours was associated in >80% of tumours with a point mutation of H-ras at the codon of the twelfth amino acid, possibly via O6-methylguanine formation causing a GC to AT transition.

raw_record.support_text: The paper states that mammary tumours can be induced in several rodent models, and that dimethylbenzanthracene (DMBA) and N-nitrosomethylurea (NMU) can produce mammary cancer in rats. These carcinogens were used to test the antitumour activity of tamoxifen, which suppressed the development of the induced mammary tumours.
raw_record.extra_details: Alias NMU; used as a carcinogen inducer in a rodent mammary tumour model.

raw_record.support_text: COX-2 protein has been detected in rat mammary tumours induced by various carcinogens, including 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazol[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP). Based on immunohistochemical analyses, COX-2 protein was observed in the epithelial cells within the mammary tumours.
raw_record.extra_details: Listed among 'various carcinogens' that induced rat mammary tumours; COX-2 protein detected within the epithelial cells of these tumours.

raw_record.support_text: The conclusions describe PhIP (2-Amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine), referred to as an environmental chemical carcinogen, as causing mammary gland carcinogenesis in rats. The mechanism involves metabolic activation and DNA adduct formation, effects on mammary gland development and proliferation, and an increase in serum prolactin secretion expected to promote tumor development; PhIP-induced carcinomas show allelic imbalance and single nucleotide instability.
raw_record.extra_details: Heterocyclic amine (HCA); PhIP-DNA adducts induce mutations though critical target genes are not yet known; PhIP also affects mammary gland development/proliferation and increases serum prolactin secretion, which is expected to promote tumor development; PhIP-induced mammary carcinomas show allelic imbalance and single nucleotide instability.

raw_record.support_text: PhIP (2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine), a chemical formed when meat-containing food is cooked, induces cancer of the colon, prostate, and mammary gland of rats (Shirai et al., 1997b).
raw_record.extra_details: PhIP; also reported to induce DNA–PhIP adducts in prostate epithelial cells transplanted into nude mice, cause growth inhibition/cell-cycle arrest, and mimic 17β-estradiol (E2) activity, suggesting a possible hormone-dependent growth pathway in prostate carcinogenesis.

raw_record.support_text: 2-Amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP), the most abundant heterocyclic amine in red meat, induces carcinomas in the mammary gland, colon and prostate of rats and lymphoma in mice.
raw_record.extra_details: PhIP is described as the most abundant heterocyclic amine in red meat. Reference citations [5,6] support this background claim.

raw_record.support_text: The cooked meat carcinogen 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP) induces tumours of the breast, colon and prostate in rats. This reports prostate tumour induction in an intact-animal carcinogenesis context.

By cDNA microarray analysis this laboratory detected elevated expression of Stat5a in rat mammary gland cancers induced by two chemical carcinogens, including 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP), a heterocyclic amine carcinogen found in the human diet in cooked meat. The study examined PhIP-induced rat mammary gland carcinomas.
raw_record.extra_details: Alias: PhIP. A heterocyclic amine carcinogen found in the human diet in cooked meat. Stat5a was evaluated in the induced carcinomas.

raw_record.support_text: 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP) induces colon tumors in rats, and is mutagenic in bacterial and mammalian cell-based genotoxicity assays.
raw_record.extra_details: PhIP is usually the most abundant HCA in cooked meat and is mutagenic in bacterial and mammalian genotoxicity assays; PhIP-DNA adducts detected in colon tissue from colon carcinoma patients.

raw_record.support_text: Heterocyclic amines are described as well recognized food-borne environmental mutagens/carcinogens, and PhIP is noted as the most abundant heterocyclic amine generated upon normal household cooking of meat. PhIP is stated to induce lymphoid tissue tumors in mice and colon, mammary gland and prostate cancers in rats [24,25].
raw_record.extra_details: Full name 2-Amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine; most abundant heterocyclic amine from normal household cooking of meat; outcome attributed to references [24,25].

raw_record.support_text: PhIP (2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine), a carcinogenic heterocyclic amine produced from overcooked foods, has been shown to induce colon tumors in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Higher CYP1A2 activity together with higher N-acetyltransferase activity has been associated with increased risk for colorectal cancer, presented as consistent with PhIP's carcinogenic activation.

raw_record.support_text: PhIP (2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine) has been demonstrated to be a genotoxic carcinogen and an oestrogen receptor ligand, and is reported in the CPDB as a Salmonella mutagen and mammary carcinogen. In the present study, analysis of the ligand MC-NC model demonstrated that PhIP was accurately predicted during the LOO validation to be a mammary carcinogen rather than a non-carcinogen.
raw_record.extra_details: Reported in the CPDB as a Salmonella mutagen and rat mammary carcinogen; described as a genotoxic carcinogen and oestrogen receptor ligand. Previous fragment-based cat-SAR analysis classified PhIP as a rat mammary carcinogen, with some carcinogenicity-related fragments not related to genotoxicity (suggesting a non-genotoxic mechanism). Ligand MC-NC model predicted PhIP as a mammary carcinogen (activity 0.64 vs cut-off 0.61) via interaction with 60 proteins including oestrogen sulfotransferase (PDB 1HY3), oestrogen receptor alpha (1X7E) and oestrogen receptor beta (1X78); MC-NMC model predicted it similarly via 21 proteins (activity 0.54 vs cut-off 0.53).

raw_record.support_text: The food-derived heterocyclic amine 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP), the most abundant heterocyclic amine in cooked meat, induces colon and mammary tumours in rats and lymphomas and hepatic tumours in mice.
raw_record.extra_details: Colon tumours produced in rats by PhIP show a high frequency of microsatellite instability similar to inherited and sporadic colorectal cancers (Canzian et al. 1994).

raw_record.support_text: The predominant heterocyclic amine formed from cooking meat at high temperatures, 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP), is described as a potent prostate carcinogen in rats. N-OH-PhIP is a substrate for and is bioactivated principally by SULT1A1 to form DNA adducts.
raw_record.extra_details: PhIP is a heterocyclic amine (HCA) formed when cooking meat at high temperatures; its N-hydroxy metabolite N-OH-PhIP is bioactivated principally by SULT1A1 to form DNA adducts. Dietary HCA exposure context.

raw_record.support_text: At least in rats, the heterocyclic aromatic amine PhIP is a colon carcinogen (Wakabayashi et al., 1992) and requires a metabolic activation event to form the proximal carcinogen.
raw_record.extra_details: Heterocyclic aromatic amine identified in cooked meat, fish, chicken and grain products; requires metabolic activation to form the proximal carcinogen. Claim attributed to Wakabayashi et al., 1992.

raw_record.support_text: COX-2 protein has been detected in rat mammary tumours induced by various carcinogens, including dimethyl-benz[a]anthracene (DMBA). Based on immunohistochemical analyses, COX-2 protein was observed in the epithelial cells within the mammary tumours.
raw_record.extra_details: Listed among 'various carcinogens' that induced rat mammary tumours; COX-2 protein detected within the epithelial cells of these tumours.

raw_record.support_text: The paper states that mammary tumours can be induced in several rodent models, and that dimethylbenzanthracene (DMBA) and N-nitrosomethylurea (NMU) can produce mammary cancer in rats. These carcinogens were used to test the antitumour activity of tamoxifen, which suppressed the development of the induced mammary tumours.
raw_record.extra_details: Alias DMBA; used as a carcinogen inducer in a rodent mammary tumour model.

raw_record.support_text: The article states that rats maintained on a soy-based diet were significantly protected against mammary tumor induction by the carcinogen dimethylbenz[a]anthracene (DMBA). It is described as a carcinogen that induces mammary tumors in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: Also referred to as DMBA; soy-based diet (and genistein) protected rats against its mammary tumor induction; DMBA-induced mammary cancer was reduced in rats given genistein neonatally or prepubertally, and genistein given from age 35 d reduced tumor multiplicity by 27% without reducing incidence.

raw_record.support_text: Recently, NTP has shown that Ni₃S₂ and NiO (green) are carcinogenic to rats. This is a positive carcinogenicity finding for nickel subsulfide in rats from the U.S. National Toxicology Program.

In the NTP studies on nickel compounds, there was a high risk of lung fibrosis in rats exposed to both nickel sulfate and nickel subsulfide, but of these only nickel subsulfide demonstrated a risk for lung cancer.
raw_record.extra_details: NTP studies; rats also showed a high risk of lung fibrosis with nickel subsulfide exposure.

raw_record.support_text: A codon 12 GGT→GTT activating mutation was found in the K-ras oncogene isolated from kidney tumors induced in rats by nickel subsulfide (Ni₃S₂). The K-ras mutation was not mandatory for nickel carcinogenesis because most tumors in the Ni₃S₂-only group lacked transforming K-ras mutations.
raw_record.extra_details: 4Ni₃S₂-induced kidney tumors carried a K-ras codon 12 GGT→GTT (glycine→valine) activating mutation; this mutation was present in only a minority of Ni₃S₂-only tumors and so was not required for tumor induction, likely contributing to tumor progression/latency.

raw_record.support_text: Studies conducted in rats have shown that brain tumors can be induced by vinyl chloride.
raw_record.extra_details: Animal studies showed neurocarcinogenicity of vinyl chloride, though reviewers noted difficulty determining whether tumors were primary or metastatic (Rice and Wilbourn, 2000).

raw_record.support_text: OSHA based the PEL reduction on the findings of Cesare Maltoni, whose studies showed induction of angiosarcoma of the liver and other organs and the production of other cancers in rats exposed to vinyl chloride. His research confirmed vinyl chloride as a carcinogen.
raw_record.extra_details: Maltoni's studies also induced angiosarcoma of other organs and produced other cancers in rats exposed to vinyl chloride. Findings supported OSHA's reduction of the permissible exposure level from 500 ppm to 50 ppm in the April 5, 1974 Emergency Temporary Standard.

raw_record.support_text: In this study, rat mammary gland carcinomas were induced by two diverse chemical carcinogens: PhIP, a heterocyclic amine found in cooked meat, and DMBA (7,12-dimethylbenz[a]anthracene), a potent experimental mammary gland carcinogen belonging to the class of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. Both compounds induced rat mammary gland carcinomas, and the resultant tumors showed distinct DNA adducts, mutation spectra, genetic alterations, and gene expression profiles.
raw_record.extra_details: A heterocyclic amine found in cooked meat. Induced rat mammary gland carcinomas that gave distinct DNA adducts, mutation spectra, and gene expression profiles relative to DMBA-induced tumors; 21 clones differed statistically between the two.

raw_record.support_text: The discovery that a proposed insecticide, 2-acetylaminofluorene (2-AAF), was carcinogenic in rats precluded its possible use against bean beetles, tobacco worms, and the like. However, 2-AAF has continued to be an important model compound in carcinogenesis research.
raw_record.extra_details: Species susceptibility varies: guinea pigs and steppe lemmings have no/low N-hydroxylating enzyme and are resistant; X/Gf mice and monkeys formed N-hydroxy derivative but appeared resistant. N-hydroxy-2-AAF derivative is more active than parent and effective in species resistant to 2-AAF; ring-hydroxylated derivatives represent detoxication products and were not carcinogenic in test animals. DNA adducts (N-(deoxyguanosin-8-yl)-2-AAF, N-(deoxyguanosin-8-yl)-2-aminofluorene, 3-(deoxyguanosin-N2-yl)-2-AAF) identified in rat liver.

raw_record.support_text: Thyroid tumors have been produced by direct-acting carcinogenic substances such as 2-acetylaminofluorene (Cox et al., 1947).
raw_record.extra_details: Described as a direct-acting carcinogenic substance.

raw_record.support_text: Five potent hepatocarcinogens—diethylnitrosamine (DEN), 2-acetylaminofluorene (2-AAF), aflatoxin B1, 3'-methyl-4-dimethylaminoazobenzene (3'-Me-DAB), and dimethylnitrosamine (DMN)—were compared using the Solt-Farber protocol to select the most appropriate initiating stimulus. Dose–response relationships regarding hyperplastic nodule numbers and areas were observed with all five carcinogens examined.
raw_record.extra_details: Called a 'potent hepatocarcinogen' in the Solt-Farber protocol comparison; dietary administration of 0.02% 2-AAF was later judged not comparable to DEN as an initiator (paras 8, 11, 26, 46).

raw_record.support_text: Macroscopically, multiple polypoid or cauliflower-shaped tumors were observed at an incidence of 100% in the MNNG-, MNUR-, BHA- and CA-treated groups. Histopathologically, the incidences of squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) were 70% in the MNNG group, 44% in the MNUR group, 11% in the BHA group and 33% in the CA group; the remaining tumors were squamous cell papillomas. No tumors were observed in the control groups.
raw_record.extra_details: N-methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine. 100% forestomach tumor incidence (70% SCC, 30% papilloma); p53 overexpression in 23%, cyclin D1 in 17%; H-ras exon 1 mutation in 67%.

raw_record.support_text: A study used the direct carcinogen N-methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine (MNNG), which reacts with DNA independently of light and oxidative processes and induces gastric carcinomas in rats. In this study, neither β-carotene nor canthaxanthin protected against MNNG-induced preneoplastic lesions, though they protected against progression of dysplasias to early and infiltrating carcinomas.
raw_record.extra_details: Called a 'direct carcinogen'; reacts with DNA independently of light and oxidative processes. Mentioned in a study evaluating whether β-carotene and canthaxanthin protect against gastric tumor progression.

raw_record.support_text: Colon tumors were induced in rats by treatment with N-methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine (MNNG), alone or with subsequent deoxycholic bile acid treatment, and tumorous versus adjacent grossly normal tissues were studied by morphological, histochemical and immunohistochemical methods.
raw_record.extra_details: MNNG-induced colon neoplasia in rats was noted to demonstrate the usefulness of morphological and histochemical methods for identifying stages of tumor development; with cell transformation, goblet cells disappeared and sialomucins and carboxyl groups appeared in transformed epithelial cells and adjacent connective tissue.

raw_record.support_text: In 1985, direct gastric carcinogenesis induced by N-methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine (MNNG) in rats was prevented in up to 70% of cases by beta-carotene or canthaxanthin diet supplementation, reporting that MNNG induces gastric carcinogenesis in rats.
raw_record.extra_details: The anticarcinogenicity of the carotenoids occurred at the progression phase, attributed to scavenging of free radicals from gastric phlogosis; carotenoids showed no protective effect against MNNG direct mutagenesis in the Ames test.

raw_record.support_text: The administration of N-methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine (MNNG), described as a carcinogen that destroys the stomach mucous barrier, constitutes a rat gastric cancer model in which animals develop benign and malignant lesions with an inflammatory cell-enriched stroma. Chemical myenteric denervation downregulated Gal-1 expression and reduced MNNG-induced GC incidence, and lowered Gal-1 had a protective role associated with reduced density of inflammatory cells.
raw_record.extra_details: MNNG is used to establish the rat gastric cancer model, producing benign and malignant lesions; destroys the stomach mucous barrier. Chemical myenteric denervation downregulated Gal-1 expression and reduced MNNG-induced gastric cancer incidence, with reduced inflammatory cell density being protective.

raw_record.support_text: The pepsinogen studies used an experimental rat gastric carcinogenesis model induced by the chemical carcinogen MNNG (N-methyl-N′-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine), described as a good model for the study of human gastric cancer. Decreased or absent PG1 protein in the rat gastric mucosa was identified from the early stage of MNNG-induced gastric carcinogenesis through to adenocarcinomas.
raw_record.extra_details: Alias MNNG; used as a model for human gastric cancer, producing gastric adenocarcinomas; associated with decreased/absent PG1 in gastric mucosa and aberrant DNA methylation of PG1.

raw_record.support_text: Across MNNG-treated groups B-E, rats developed malignant small intestinal tumors. Histologically these were carcinosarcomas or well-to-moderately differentiated (and several poorly differentiated) adenocarcinomas, some mucinous with desmoplasia; animals with small bowel cancer per group were 6/9 (B), 4/12 (C), 7/13 (D), and 9/12 (E). Control groups A and F, which received no MNNG, had no small bowel tumors.
raw_record.extra_details: N-methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine (MNNG); 39-week study. Small intestinal tumors included one carcinosarcoma in the group, and in group E five rats had adhesions between tumors, liver, and intestines. No statistically significant differences in small bowel cancer incidence among MNNG-treated groups B-E.

raw_record.support_text: In the Discussion, the authors note that several chemicals have been found to induce gastric adenocarcinomas in the rat glandular stomach, and that the most potent compound is N-methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine (MNNG), which has been utilized as a highly effective experimental model for studying gastric carcinogenesis.

raw_record.support_text: Azoxymethane (AOM) induces both aberrant crypt foci (ACF) and tumors in rats, and AOM-induced colon carcinogenesis is a widely used model for studying the multistage development of cancer. The AOM model is described as an important tool for identifying early molecular changes and testing preventive vaccines.
raw_record.extra_details: Abbreviation AOM. Induces ACF (precancerous colon lesions) and colon tumors; AOM-induced colon carcinogenesis model. K-ras mutation frequencies of 7-32% observed in AOM-induced colon cancers and ACF.

raw_record.support_text: Colon carcinogenesis induced in the rat by azoxymethane or 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) is used as a model mimicking the histopathological and molecular alterations observed in human colorectal pathology. In this experimental setting, precancerous lesions such as Mucin Depleted Foci are studied as the earliest alterations preceding colon tumour development.
raw_record.extra_details: Used as an experimental inducer of rat colon carcinogenesis to mimic human colorectal cancer sequence; study of precancerous Mucin Depleted Foci lesions.

raw_record.support_text: In animal experiments, a few doses of azoxymethane (AOM) can induce multicentric colon tumors in a short period of time (cites 102, 148). Diets containing 23.5 percent safflower or corn oil fed to rats exposed to AOM result in significantly higher proportions of animals with colon tumors than do diets of 23.5 percent coconut or olive oil. AOM is referred to as a colon carcinogen in this context.
raw_record.extra_details: A few doses suffice to induce tumors in a short period of time; fat feeding modifies the resulting colon tumor incidence; passage refers to AOM among colon carcinogens.

raw_record.support_text: 1,2-dimethylhydrazine/azoxymethane- (DMH/AOM-) induced colon carcinogenesis is described as a multistep process in rats, with morphological and histological features similar to human sporadic colon carcinogenesis, and the main cellular and molecular defects of human colon carcinogenesis are also observed in DMH/AOM rat colon carcinogenesis.
raw_record.extra_details: Used together with 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) as DMH/AOM; model reproduces multistep colon carcinogenesis with Wnt, K-ras, TGFβ, and inflammatory pathway alterations.

raw_record.support_text: In vivo rat studies examined the effect of oral silymarin after exposure to the carcinogenic agent azoxymethane, which induces adenocarcinoma in the colon. Silymarin reduced the frequency of precancerous changes and, with longer follow-up, the incidence and multiplicity of carcinoma.
raw_record.extra_details: Described as carcinogenic ('kancerogenní'); induces colon adenocarcinoma. Silymarin given per os after azoxymethane exposure reduced precancerous lesions and carcinoma incidence/multiplicity.

raw_record.support_text: Tumors induced by AOM (azoxymethane) were found only in the colon in AOM-treated rats. In rats given AOM with normal rat chow pellet, colon cancers were found in 8 of 16 rats (50.0%), while in rats given AOM with a chemically defined diet, the incidence was significantly higher (14/15, 93.3%). Incidence was 93.3% (14/15) with a chemically defined diet vs 50.0% (8/16) with normal rat chow, a significant difference; roughly 59% of tumors in the defined-diet group were highly differentiated adenocarcinomas. Diet/carcinogen exposure is the study focus; no formal carcinogenicity classification reported.

raw_record.support_text: Nigro et al. The carcinogen azoxymethane induced intestinal tumors in these rats.

raw_record.support_text: Ferric nitrilotriacetate (Fe-NTA), an iron chelate, induces renal proximal tubular damage via a Fenton-like reaction in vivo, which ultimately leads to a high incidence of renal cell carcinoma (RCC) in rodents. raw_record.extra_details: Fe-NTA administration caused oxidative tubular damage and, after repeated administration, induced renal cell carcinomas (RCCs). raw_record.extra_details: Carcinogenesis is attributed to Fenton reaction-based repeated oxidative stress; induced genetic alterations reported as similar to those in human RCC.

raw_record.support_text: Modern research on chemical carcinogenesis began with the isolation of benzo[a]pyrene (B[a]P) from coal tar in 1930 and the demonstration that B[a]P and several synthetic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) induced tumors upon repeated painting on mouse skin. raw_record.support_text: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, for example benzopyrene, were identified as chemical carcinogens, and benzopyrene was shown to be carcinogenic in mouse skin by Cook, Hewett, and Hieger in 1933. This explicitly reports that benzo(a)pyrene is carcinogenic in mouse skin.

raw_record.support_text: In 1933 Heiger isolated benzo[a]pyrene (B[a]P) from coal tar and found it to be highly carcinogenic on mouse skin; the synthesized material was also found to be highly tumorigenic on mouse skin.

raw_record.support_text: Cook and Hewett synthesized the then unknown compounds benzo(a)pyrene (BP) and benzo(e)pyrene and found them identical with the major and minor components, respectively, of the mixed crystals isolated from coal tar. raw_record.extra_details: Identified as the major component of the coal tar carcinogen; both synthetic and isolated samples were 'highly carcinogenic'; results published in April 1933 by Cook, Hewett and Hieger; alias BP.
